concept.name: Market-impact model
concept.definition: A model of price movement caused by the strategy's own trading, often separated into temporary and persistent components.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Estimate impact from participation, order size, volatility, liquidity, execution time, and calibrated coefficients; feed it into simulated fills and later prices if modeled.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A 10% participation order receives more impact than a 1% participation order in the same stock and volatility regime.
